candidates.source_name: Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle)
candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 17:11 (Akedah preamble (17:11)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And Sarah said to Abraham: cast out this bondwoman and her son, for the son of this bondwoman will not be heir with my son, with Isaac' — Jubilees follows the Genesis 21 sequence: Sarah's demand, Abraham's grief, the divine ratification (17:6, 'in Isaac shall thy seed be called'). Tewahedo readings sharpen this scene against any Marcionite anti-Jewish reading: Ishmael is NOT cursed (17:20, God promises to bless him with twelve princes) but he is NOT the line of covenant-bearing seed. The Tewahedo distinction between general-providential blessing (extended to all Abraham's descendants) and elect-covenant blessing (channeled through Isaac then Jacob) draws canonical warrant here.

candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And it came to pass in the seventh week, in the first year thereof, in the first month in this jubilee, on the twelfth of this month, there were voices in heaven regarding Abraham, that he was faithful in all that He told him, and that he loved the Lord, and that in every affliction he was faithful' — Jubilees places the Mastema accusation against Abraham at the precise date of the future Passover (the first month, twelfth day — eve of Nisan 14). Tewahedo Pascha (Fasika) liturgy reads this as the canonical placement: the Akedah is offered AS PASSOVER, not merely typologically connected. Mastema's accusation against the faithful one is overthrown on the same date that the Lamb defeats the firstborn-slaying angel of Ex 12 — typological inversion preserved in Tewahedo Holy-Week chant.

candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And in every test which He had tested him he was found faithful, and his soul was not impatient, and he was not slow to act, for he was faithful and a lover of the Lord' — Jubilees ascribes to Abraham a settled disposition of patient faithful love (a hapax phrase in Charles, 'a lover of the Lord' / Ge'ez 'mafqäre ǝgziʾabəḥer'). Tewahedo monastic ideal preserves this Jubilees phrase as the goal of contemplative life: not merely obedient service but loving disposition that makes the soul un-impatient under repeated testing. Maḫǝbär Qǝddus (holy-fellowship monastic order) draws its charism from this verse: 'lovers-of-the-Lord' is the Tewahedo monastic self-designation.
